summary: The r3 commit preserves the chatbot API responses and package entry exports. The IM3 PII stripper can also delete non-PII lesson content after a matching label.
blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] review-c: `stripPersonDetails` removes all text from any `Student:`, `Name:`, or other matching label through the next matching label or end of lesson markdown. This can remove later instructional content from the prompt and change the chatbot answer beyond removing person details. Rationale: the pattern at `apps/integrated-math-3/app/api/student/lesson-chatbot/route.ts:36-56` spans arbitrary content, while the adversarial test checks only content before the first label.
evidence: F1 withdrawn: packages/ai-tutoring/src/__tests__/index-exports.test.ts imports and calls AI_ROLES, resolveRoleModel, buildProviderPreferences, and AiRole from the package entry point.
The r3 commit e5680156 does not change packages/ai-tutoring/src/index.ts; the current entry point retains the four planned additions at line 15.

Both chatbot routes still return { error: 'AI provider not configured' } with status 503 when the role provider is unavailable: apps/bus-math-v2/app/api/student/lesson-chatbot/route.ts:185-187 and apps/integrated-math-3/app/api/student/lesson-chatbot/route.ts:234-236.

Both routes retain their prior error response bodies and statuses: BM2 returns the fixed 502 body at route.ts:193-196; IM3 returns the fixed 500 body at route.ts:242-245. The r3 changes only provider role resolution and log fields in these response paths.
The IM3 S2 adversarial test asserts a 200 response body of { response: 'Try factoring.' } and verifies ordinary lesson text reaches the provider at route.s2.adversarial.test.ts:115-127.

The IM3 stripper matches labeled details across arbitrary text at route.ts:36-56. The adversarial fixture verifies math text only before the first label at route.s2.adversarial.test.ts:92-97, so it does not prove lesson content after a label survives.
The prior review's export-contract finding is withdrawn: the package-entry test covers all four planned exports.
